---
title: "Lectures"
subtitle: "Recorded lectures and student lecture notes"
---

Every row links to the recorded lecture video and to whichever sets of student
lecture notes cover that lecture. Use the search box to filter by topic, and
click a column header to sort.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")

import pandas as pd
import coursesite as S

lectures = S.load("lectures")
meta = S.load("meta")

df = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {
            "Lec": lec["lec_no"],
            "Lecture": lec["name"],
            "Video": S.video_cell(lec["videos"]),
            "Notes": S.notes_cell(lec["notes"], meta["notes_sets"]),
        }
        for lec in lectures
    ]
)

S.show_table(
    df,
    columnDefs=[
        {"width": "3rem", "targets": 0},
        {"width": "34%", "targets": 1},
        {"orderable": False, "targets": [2, 3]},
    ],
)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## About these materials

Videos are the Cornell recordings of **MAE 4730/5730**. The note sets are
student-taken notes from different offerings, so they cover different subsets
of the syllabus — a lecture may have notes from one set, both, or neither.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
lines = []
for label in meta["notes_sets"]:
    n = sum(1 for lec in lectures for x in lec["notes"] if x["set"] == label)
    lines.append(f"- **{S.short_set_name(label)}** — `{label}` ({n} lecture links)")
print("\n".join(lines))
```
:::
